result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-023.md for WF02-REQ-023 (waitlist auto-promotion on a freed seat, halting at T-24h) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-023, commit fb57234. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's new isAutoPromotionHalted; apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts's new decidePromotionEligibility/promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible, extended WithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration, new getEventIdForRegistration; apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts's new getUserForNotificationById; apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts's new sendPromotionNotification and its call site; apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts's new Catalog.promotion section) is real user-visible/behavioral surface -- a real Telegram message sent to a different chat than the one that triggered the withdrawal, real registrations/audit_log writes, and a real seat-accounting guarantee under concurrency. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md Step 3, docs/guides/qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-022.md (reference shape/harness), docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md in full, the real implementations of isAutoPromotionHalted (domain/event.ts line ~744), decidePromotionEligibility/promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible/the extended withdrawRegistration (domain/registration.ts lines 313-565), getUserForNotificationById (domain/user.ts lines 143-179), and handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification and confirm-callback wiring in full -- plus BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/domain/registration.db.test.ts lines 845-1207 (AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC7 domain-level cases plus decidePromotionEligibility's own unit table) and apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts lines 316-460 (AC6 and the S10/AC8 blocked-user dispatch-level cases) -- so this spec's cases are independently parameterized, not accidental duplicates, and so the gap analysis is grounded in what is actually committed rather than assumed.

All 7 stated ACs plus the implicit AC8 (blocked promoted user: DB-level success, no notification, established during the security-fix cycle) each have at least one concrete, judgment-free verification case. None merely re-points at BACKEND-DEV's coverage -- every case is this spec's own, with its own uuids and its own tg_id range 1000000600+ (distinct from REQ-019/020/021/022's own ranges and from both existing test files' internal sequence counters).

Gaps closed, case-by-case:
- AC1: BACKEND-DEV's case inserts its 3 waitlisted rows via direct db.insert() and calls withdrawRegistration directly. This spec's case creates all 4 registrations (seat-holder + 3 waitlisted) through real register: callbacks, withdraws through a real /withdraw + withdraw:confirm dispatch, and checks via SQL that the two untouched candidates' admission/qr_token are unchanged and that the promotion notification is sent to exactly the earliest candidate's chat, never the other two's.
- AC2 + AC2-boundary: BACKEND-DEV's case uses a 12h-out event, comfortably inside the halt window. This run's own instruction called for the EXACT T-24h boundary, never tested anywhere in this codebase -- added as its own AC2-boundary case: a pure-function test of isAutoPromotionHalted at exactly T-24h (expect halted=true, matching the real `<=` comparison read directly from domain/event.ts) and at T-24h-minus-1-second/24h-plus-1s-remaining (expect halted=false), plus a live-dispatch corroboration noting the dispatch-level test can only approximate exact-instant precision (the real withdrawRegistration call uses `new Date()`, not an injectable evaluationTime) while the pure-function case gives true millisecond control.
- AC3: BACKEND-DEV's case calls withdrawRegistration directly. This spec's case dispatches a real /withdraw + confirm cycle against an empty waitlist, asserting bot.handleUpdate resolves without throwing, exactly one ordinary confirmedReply is sent, and zero registration.promote audit rows exist.
- AC4: BACKEND-DEV's case is a single promotion racing a single fresh registration, capacity=1, both via direct domain calls, 20 iterations. Per this run's explicit instruction, this spec's case uses a materially different shape: capacity=3, TWO concurrent withdrawals (each independently capable of triggering its own promotion) racing TWO concurrent fresh registrations for the same event, all four dispatched through real bot.handleUpdate() calls, 5 iterations (a named, justified trade-off against the harness's higher per-iteration dispatch cost, since the property under test -- the events-row FOR UPDATE lock serializing all contenders -- is exercised structurally by even one iteration). Pass condition: admitted count is exactly 3 (never 4+, never <3) every iteration.
- AC5: BACKEND-DEV's case calls promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible directly against a pre-broken event. This spec's case cancels a real event AFTER a real registration filled it and a real waitlist formed, then withdraws via a real dispatch, confirming the withdrawer's own confirmedReply is unaffected by the promotion's silent underlying refusal (no error, no promotion, no notification).
- AC6: already fully covered at the dispatch level by BACKEND-DEV's own withdraw.test.ts case (real bot.handleUpdate, broadcast_opt_in=false, promotion sendMessage confirmed sent to the promoted person's own chat). This spec explicitly declines to add a redundant re-parameterization here (would close no gap) and instead notes AC1/AC4's own cases corroborate the same send-to-promoted-chat mechanism under different fixtures.
- AC7: BACKEND-DEV's two cases are (a) one genuine promotion's audit-row count and (b) two calls against an event that was full FROM THE START, never actually freed. This spec's own case genuinely frees a seat once via a real dispatch (counting the actual single sendMessage to the promoted chat), then calls promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible a SECOND time against that now-refilled event, gets capacity-full with zero new audit rows, and states the structural argument (sendPromotionNotification's one call site is gated on outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted', which the second run's capacity-full result can never satisfy) for why a second notification is impossible, not merely asserted.
- AC8 (implicit, from the S10 security-fix cycle): already covered at the dispatch level by BACKEND-DEV's own S10 rework case (single waitlisted candidate, blocked, promotion completes at the DB level with one audit row, zero notification sends). This spec's own case uses a materially different, multi-candidate shape: capacity=2, TWO waitlisted candidates where the EARLIER-created one is blocked and a LATER-created one is not -- proving the blocked-skip applies only to the notification (the blocked candidate is still admitted with a fresh qr_token and exactly one audit row) and never re-routes the freed seat to the non-blocked candidate as a substitute (who correctly remains waitlisted, since only one seat was freed).

Also added AC-schema (git diff --stat on apps/bot/drizzle, confirmed empty on commit fb57234, matching the design's explicit no-schema-change claim) and AC-catalog (grep-based parity check of the 3 new Catalog.promotion keys across types.ts/ru.ts/en.ts, with an explicit note that TEST-RUNNER must distinguish promotion.whatNext's occurrence from registration.whatNext's pre-existing one rather than raw-counting matches), per this project's REQ-020/021/022 precedent of covering mechanical claims beyond the numbered ACs.

Noted ISS-0014's --no-file-parallelism requirement in the spec's own execution-note section, and pointed TEST-RUNNER at REQ-020.md's Shared Setup step 6 for the live-dispatch harness boilerplate rather than re-pasting a fourth copy of the same script.

Gap found while reading: none beyond what this run's own instructions already named and this spec closes. No design or implementation defect found -- nothing new to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
